pathophysiology.summary: Loss of effective cardiac mechanical activity stops systemic perfusion. Shockable VF/pVT may respond to defibrillation; asystole and PEA require CPR and treatment of reversible causes. High-quality compressions and minimal interruptions maintain coronary and cerebral perfusion until ROSC.
keyMechanisms: Loss of effective cardiac mechanical activity stops systemic perfusion.
Shockable VF/pVT may respond to defibrillation; asystole and PEA require CPR and treatment of reversible causes.
High-quality compressions and minimal interruptions maintain coronary and cerebral perfusion until ROSC.

ruleOut.testName: Point-of-care glucose, blood gas and electrolytes
ruleOut.modalityTarget: During resuscitation when sampling is feasible
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Hypoglycaemia, severe potassium abnormality, hypoxaemia or marked acid-base disturbance
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Identify and immediately correct a reversible metabolic cause without interrupting high-quality CPR.
ruleOut.normalValue: Glucose 3.9–10 mmol/L; potassium 3.5–5.0 mmol/L; no severe acid-base disturbance

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise and start CPR
actions: Activate the resuscitation team, start high-quality CPR, attach defibrillator and give oxygen.

clinicalManagement.title: Rhythm-directed ALS
actions: Shock VF/pVT and resume CPR immediately; give epinephrine and amiodarone according to the algorithm.
For asystole/PEA give epinephrine as soon as feasible and continue CPR.

clinicalManagement.title: Treat causes and transition
actions: Treat reversible Hs and Ts; after ROSC move to post-cardiac-arrest care.

adjustments: The AHA arrest algorithm gives no renal or hepatic adjustment; follow the resuscitation protocol.
monitoring: Rhythm and pulse checks every 2 minutes; continuous waveform capnography when an advanced airway is present.
contraindications: No contraindication is listed in the cardiac-arrest algorithm.

regimens.indication: Refractory ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia
regimens.dose: First dose 300 mg; second dose 150 mg
regimens.frequency: One first dose, then one second dose if refractory
adjustments: No renal or hepatic adjustment is specified for arrest dosing in the algorithm; do not delay defibrillation.
monitoring: Rhythm after each 2-minute CPR cycle; ROSC and adverse haemodynamics after conversion.
contraindications: Use only for refractory VF/pVT in this algorithm.
